elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 11 as rendered: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof." The prior "laws of the Arizona" is replaced; no competing choice-of-law sentence remains.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Section 19 as rendered: all "Disputes" "will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, New York, provided that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." Mandatory binding arbitration under the U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules and the award-confirmation sentence are deleted, so the merits forum is exclusively NY County courts with only a temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out, which the rule expressly preserves.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 11 selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is expected because the drafter targeted the preferred level; the fallback is simply not the level pursued.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 19 designates the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware/California courts or the courts of London. Again, this reflects targeting of the preferred level rather than a defect.

elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Element belongs to the preferred checklist only; assessed above as met at the preferred level.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the choice-of-law words in Section 11 were swapped from Arizona to the State of New York, and Section 19 now confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County over all defined "Disputes," with the only carve-out being temporary injunctive relief in another court of competent jurisdiction — the customary carve-out the rule permits.

Walk-away risk (mandatory arbitration under U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules) is eliminated in operative text, not merely promised in the comment; the arbitral award-confirmation sentence was removed so no arbitration mechanic survives to contradict the new court forum.

Minimality holds: the severability sentence, the conflict-of-laws tail, the Dispute definition and its (b)/(c) limbs, and the execution block are all retained verbatim; the only other change is the Section 19 heading from "Arbitration" to "Jurisdiction," which is necessary to avoid a dangling arbitration reference once the arbitration mechanic is deleted, and is therefore not cosmetic surplus. No survival tails, fee-shifting, procedures, or other extras were added.

Intent preserved: no undefined terms or dangling cross-references result — "Disputes" remains defined in the same sentence, and "Except as otherwise specified below" continues to operate against the retained proviso; no retained sentence contradicts the exclusive court forum.

Fallback elements are not met, but that is immaterial to position-completeness because the redline lands squarely at the preferred level; the comment correctly offers Delaware, California, or England and Wales with London courts as an acceptable fallback without leaving it as the operative text.
